title: The 10 Best Infrared Thermometers
subtitle: Infrared temperature guns for HVAC, electrical, automotive and cooking, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An infrared thermometer reads surface temperature instantly from a distance, for anything from a breaker panel to a pizza stone. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Fluke, Klein Tools, Etekcity, TempPro and value brands on rating, review volume and features (adjustable emissivity, 12:1 or better distance-to-spot, a range over 1,000°F and max/min readings).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

products.name: Etekcity Lasergrip 1080 Infrared Thermometer, -58 to 1130°F
products.best_for: Cooks, mechanics and HVAC DIYers who want accurate readings on any surface.
products.verdict: Etekcity's step up: adjustable emissivity for accurate readings on different surfaces, a range to 1130°F for pizza ovens, and a max-temperature display.

products.name: TempPro TempScan Infrared Thermometer Gun (TP30)
products.best_for: Pizza oven and griddle cooks who also check HVAC vents.
products.verdict: Adjustable emissivity, MAX/MIN/AVG readings, a stated ±1.5% accuracy and a range to 1022°F, with 9,853 reviews.

products.name: TempPro TempScan PLUS TP450 Infrared Thermometer with 2 Lasers
products.best_for: Grill and pizza oven cooks who want a tighter spot.
products.verdict: TempPro's upgraded gun with dual lasers that frame the spot, a tighter 16:1 ratio, adjustable emissivity and MAX/MIN/AVG.

products.name: Etekcity Lasergrip 774 Infrared Thermometer
products.best_for: Checking griddles, ovens, AC vents and engines at home.
products.verdict: The best-selling and most-reviewed thermometer here: 12:1 distance-to-spot, -58 to 842°F and a backlit screen, for under $20.

products.name: Klein Tools IR10 Infrared Thermometer with Dual Targeting Laser, 20:1, K-Type Probe
products.best_for: HVAC techs measuring duct air and refrigerant lines.
products.verdict: Klein's top model: 20:1 for small or distant targets, a range to 1200°F, and a K-type probe for measuring air, gas and liquid that IR can't read.

specs.extras: K-type probe for air, gas and liquid; alarms; max/min/avg/diff

products.name: Klein Tools IR5 Infrared Thermometer with Dual Targeting Laser, 12:1
products.best_for: HVAC and electrical techs who want alarms and statistics.
products.verdict: A pro Klein with dual lasers, adjustable emissivity, max/min/avg/difference readings and high and low alarms.

specs.extras: Dual lasers, auto scan, max/min/avg/diff, high/low alarm

products.name: KNINE OUTDOORS Infrared Thermometer Gun, -58 to 1112°F (TG-2024-OG)
products.best_for: Pizza oven cooks on a budget.
products.verdict: A 12:1 thermometer that reads up to 1112°F, high enough for pizza ovens, for under $20.

products.name: Fluke 62 Max Industrial Infrared Thermometer, -22 to 932°F, IP54
products.best_for: Maintenance techs who need a thermometer that survives the job.
products.verdict: Fluke's industrial thermometer: IP54 dust and water resistance, a stated ±1.5% accuracy, and a 3-year warranty, rated 4.7 stars.

products.name: Soonkoda GM50 Digital Infrared Thermometer, -58 to 932°F

products.name: Klein Tools IR1 Infrared Thermometer with Targeting Laser
products.best_for: Electricians checking breakers, connections and motors.
products.verdict: Klein's basic IR thermometer for electricians and HVAC techs: 10:1, -4 to 752°F, and a fixed 0.95 emissivity that suits most non-shiny surfaces.

specs.extras: Laser targeting, backlit display, auto power off

avoid.name: SURPEER Infrared Thermometer Temperature Gun, -58 to 1796°F, 50:1
avoid.verdict: A $40 thermometer claiming a 50:1 distance-to-spot ratio, two and a half times Klein's $115 IR10 and five times Fluke's 62 Max.
reasons: It claims '50:1 distance-to-spot ratio'. Klein's top IR10 is 20:1 and Fluke's industrial 62 Max is 10:1.
No accuracy figure is given to back the 50:1 or the 1796°F range.

The model number is written in decorative bold Unicode characters and the part number is a random string, so the exact product is hard to identify. The TempPro TP450 lists a 16:1 ratio and ±1.5% accuracy for less.

buyers_guide.a: D:S tells you how big the measured spot is at a distance. At 12:1, from 12 inches away you read a 1-inch circle. Higher ratios read smaller or farther targets.
IR thermometers assume a surface emits heat like a matte object (about 0.95). Shiny metal like stainless or aluminum reads low. Adjustable emissivity, or a piece of tape on the surface, fixes that.

buyers_guide.q: Can it read air or liquid temperature?
buyers_guide.a: No. IR reads surfaces only. For air in a duct or liquid in a pot, use a probe; Klein's IR10 includes one.
752°F covers electrical, HVAC and engines. Pizza ovens and forges need 900°F to 1,100°F or more.
These are surface thermometers for objects. They aren't calibrated for body temperature.
